title: Console retention settings UX: IA, copy, error states, and legal hold messaging
creator: Tessa Morgan
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: Retention controls + compliance reporting pack
description:
## Why
Enterprise prospects are asking for tenant-configurable retention controls and proof they are enforced. We need a Console UX that:
- Makes retention settings discoverable and understandable for admins
- Shows the *effective policy* (with precedence/overrides) and guardrails
- Clearly communicates what is in-scope for v1 (and what is not)
- Explains legal holds and exceptions without causing confusion/panic
- Provides auditability (who changed what/when) and enforcement status

This ticket covers information architecture, UX copy, UI states, error states, and legal hold messaging for the Retention Controls page.

## Target users
- Org Admin / Security Admin managing retention posture
- Solutions Engineer / auditor reviewing evidence during a security review

## Entry points / IA
Proposed nav:
- Console → Settings → Security & Compliance → **Data retention**

Secondary entry points:
- Security & Compliance overview page → “Configure retention” CTA
- Audit Logs page banner (if retention differs from default): “Retention controlled in Data retention settings”

## Primary UX requirements (v1)
### 1) Retention settings page layout
**Page structure**
1. Page header: “Data retention”
   - Short subtext: “Configure how long Redwood stores operational datasets for your tenant. Some datasets are governed by platform/SRE defaults.”
2. Environment selector (if applicable): Production / Staging (Private deployments may have different env concepts; keep design flexible)
3. Dataset table/cards (grouped by category)
   - Audit logs
   - Admin activity (Console/admin actions)
   - Inference request metadata (not raw prompts/responses)
   - Telemetry/analytics (eligible tables only)
   - Operational logs (where applicable)
4. Right rail / details drawer (recommended) for per-dataset configuration and explanations
5. "Enforcement status" panel (per dataset)
6. "Change history" link (admin audit trail)

**Dataset rows should show at-a-glance:**
- Dataset name
- Retention duration (effective)
- Source of policy (Default / Tenant setting / Legal hold / Exception)
- Last enforcement run + status (Success / Degraded / Not yet run)
- Export availability (e.g., Audit logs export supported)

### 2) Effective policy + precedence messaging (copy)
We need to reduce confusion when users set a value but see a different effective value due to guardrails or higher-precedence policies.

Copy patterns:
- “Effective retention” (what will actually be enforced)
- “Configured retention” (what the admin attempted to set)
- “Reason” / “Why this value?” tooltip

Reason examples:
- “Adjusted to minimum allowed (30 days) by your plan’s guardrails.”
- “Overridden by legal hold applied on 2025-02-03.”
- “Inherited from Organization default.” (If we later support org-level defaults vs tenant-level; for v1 we can simplify but keep wording future-proof.)

### 3) Guardrails + validation states
Guardrails are enforced server-side (ENG-2911/2912), but the UI must proactively guide users.

Required UI states:
- Inline validation for min/max with exact numbers: “Must be between 30 and 365 days.”
- If user enters an out-of-range value and saves:
  - Block save and show error returned by API (preferred)
  - OR auto-clamp and show a non-dismissable warning: “We saved 30 days (minimum allowed).” (Only if Product explicitly wants clamping; default recommendation is **block** to avoid surprise.)
- If legal hold is present:
  - Disable retention input (read-only)
  - Show banner explaining hold and next step (see Legal Hold section)

### 4) Enforcement status visibility
We need a compact, non-technical “proof” surface that is still honest about limitations.

Per dataset show:
- “Last run:” timestamp + relative time
- “Deleted in last 24h:” count (if available)
- “Backlog:” optional (only if meaningful and not alarming)
- Link: “View details” (goes to a technical drawer/modal with job id, region, and guidance)

If status is degraded (e.g., backlog building):
- Warning state with copy that avoids implying data loss:
  - “Retention enforcement is delayed. Data may be retained longer than configured until processing catches up.”
  - CTA: “View status” + optional link to support

### 5) Legal hold messaging (must be unambiguous)
Legal hold semantics:
- It pauses deletion for impacted datasets, retaining data beyond configured retention.
- It should be treated as higher precedence than tenant retention settings.

UX requirements:
- **Top-of-page banner** when any hold applies:
  - Title: “Legal hold is active”
  - Body: “Deletion is paused for one or more datasets while a legal hold is active. Retention settings cannot be reduced until the hold is removed.”
  - Secondary text: “Legal holds are managed by Redwood support for now.” (v1 assumption)
  - CTA: “Contact support” (opens prefilled support ticket) / “Learn more” (docs)
- Per-dataset indicator badge: “On hold”
- In dataset details drawer:
  - Show hold scope and start date (if available)
  - Show who requested it (if available; otherwise “Set by Redwood”) and a reference id

Copy tone guidance:
- Avoid legal advice; avoid panic language (“frozen”, “seized”).
- Be explicit about user impact: “Data will not be deleted on schedule.”

### 6) Auditability / change history
Admins and auditors will ask “who changed retention?” Provide a consistent pattern:
- Link “View change history” showing:
  - Timestamp
  - Actor
  - Dataset
  - Old → new value
  - Reason/notes (optional)

We should align with Console audit logging patterns (if existing): same table component, same filters.

## Deliverables
- IA recommendation (where this lives in Console + entry points)
- Component spec for dataset list + details drawer
- Copy deck (microcopy for headers/tooltips/banners/errors)
- Error/empty/loading states
- Legal hold banner + per-row badges
- Handoff notes for ENG-2926 (Console backend endpoints) and ENG Console UI implementation

## References / links
- Google Drive: Console retention settings wireframe slides (draft): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/console-retention-settings-wireframe-slides.json
- Confluence overview: Retention controls overview: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-controls-overview.json
- Policy engine/schema: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-policy-schema-and-evaluation.json
- Support/Sales FAQ (for consistent language): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/retention-controls-and-compliance-reporting-faq.json

## Open questions
1) Should the UI allow *increasing* retention beyond default without support (subject to max), or is any change gated?
2) Are we showing per-region enforcement status in Hosted/Dedicated? If not, what do we say for multi-region tenants?
3) Do we need separate settings for Dedicated vs Hosted if a tenant has both?
4) Do we explicitly label datasets that are out of scope (e.g., “Operational logs (platform-managed)”)? Recommendation: yes, but keep the list short and link to docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- Users can find the Data retention page under Settings → Security & Compliance
- For each v1 dataset, users can see effective retention, where it comes from, and whether changes are blocked by hold/guardrails
- Legal hold messaging is clear, action-oriented, and consistent across page + dataset drawer
- Error states are specified for: permission denied, validation errors, backend unavailable, status unknown, initial loading/empty
- Copy is reviewed by Product (Naomi Feldman, Marissa Cole) and Security Eng (Marcus Lin) for accuracy

comments: Naomi Feldman (2025-01-23): Please do not say we offer customer-configurable retention for inference content. We should explicitly scope to metadata and audit logs for v1. Add a short sentence near the top of the page clarifying this.

Chloe Martin (2025-01-27): For enforcement status, we can reliably provide last-run timestamp and success/failure. Counts/backlog may not be in v1 for all datasets—design should make those optional fields so we can hide when unavailable.

Marcus Lin (2025-01-29): Legal hold messaging must be precise: deletion is paused; data may be retained longer. Avoid “data is stored indefinitely” unless that is truly the case. Also ensure permission model: only Security Admins see the support CTA.
Marissa Cole (2025-02-06): Let’s add an info box: “Retention changes may take up to 24 hours to fully apply” (confirm with SRE). Also add a link to audit log exports from the Audit logs dataset row.
Jada Williams (2025-02-21): Drawer pattern is fine. For error states, please include permission-denied copy that instructs user to contact an Org Admin/Security Admin, since RBAC will be strict.
